description: Context-loaded, non-executable discipline-specific validation playbooks, for native delegation by Codex

A00.name: guardian_engineering_orchestrator
checkpoints: Decompose intent into a minimal acyclic task plan with explicit stop conditions.
Separate known facts, assumptions, constraints and human approval gates.
Keep one owner for each write-critical scope; record all blocked or unverified work.

S01.name: guardian_product_discovery
checkpoints: Validate the user problem with stakeholders and observable evidence.
Prioritize outcomes, cost of delay, competing hypotheses and narrow MVP scope.
Define metrics and acceptance owners; avoid invented market validation.

S02.name: guardian_requirements_engineer
checkpoints: Trace functional and nonfunctional requirements to acceptance cases.
Specify positive, negative, edge and unauthorized user journeys.
Identify ambiguous business rules and invariants before coding.

S03.name: guardian_solutions_architect
checkpoints: Map as-is components, trust boundaries, data flows and third-party dependencies.
Compare architecture alternatives via explicit ADR and failure assumptions.
Validate compatibility, criticality, reliability, operating cost and reversibility.

S04.name: guardian_frontend_architect
checkpoints: Inspect actual component boundaries, state ownership and rendering pipeline.
Evaluate route transitions, error states, caching and shared UI contracts.
Check accessibility and behavior in relevant browsers before broad refactoring.

S05.name: guardian_frontend_engineer
checkpoints: Implement narrowly scoped responsive UI behavior preserving design and state boundaries.
Test keyboard, loading, validation, empty and error paths.
Keep API assumptions and component interface compatibility explicit.

S06.name: guardian_ux_accessibility
checkpoints: Audit semantics, labels, focus order, keyboard access and screen-reader context.
Validate contrast, responsive layouts and error announcements against applicable WCAG criteria.
Distinguish static findings from tests requiring assistive technology.

S07.name: guardian_web_performance
checkpoints: Measure LCP, INP, CLS and resource waterfalls before optimization.
Check hydration, caching, SSR/CSR behavior and browser compatibility.
Report reproducible before/after metrics and test configuration.

S08.name: guardian_backend_domain
checkpoints: Trace request execution, domain invariants, side effects and exception boundaries.
Preserve transaction semantics, nullability, async cancellation and DI lifetimes.
Verify normal, negative and integration boundary behavior.

S09.name: guardian_api_integration
checkpoints: Map producers, consumers, versions, authentication and error contracts.
Check OpenAPI drift, pagination, rate limits, retries and webhook integrity.
Prove compatible or intentionally versioned changes using contract tests.

S10.name: guardian_distributed_concurrency
checkpoints: Analyze atomicity, event ordering, deduplication, concurrency and failure windows.
Review idempotency, outbox/inbox, saga and reconciliation patterns only when justified.
Test race conditions, message redelivery and partial failure recovery.

S11.name: guardian_database_transactions
checkpoints: Validate schema, constraints, isolation, indexes and query plans in context.
Simulate expand/migrate/contract upgrades and rollback limitations.
Check integrity invariants and operational migration risk.

S12.name: guardian_data_governance
checkpoints: Map lineage, data owners, quality checks, retention and classification.
Verify backup and restore assumptions with actual evidence.
Flag privacy, disposal and access-control omissions.

S13.name: guardian_appsec
checkpoints: Derive threat model from assets, actors, entry points and trust boundaries.
Verify OWASP-relevant vulnerabilities and mitigation effectiveness safely.
Prioritize reproducible security findings with exploit preconditions and residual risk.

S14.name: guardian_iam_privacy
checkpoints: Trace identities, grants, audience/scopes, session lifecycle and tenant boundaries.
Test access-denied flows, OIDC/JWT validation and authorization enforcement.
Evaluate LGPD-impacting data flows and never request credentials.

S15.name: guardian_cloud_supply_security
checkpoints: Assess supply chain provenance, SBOM, locked dependencies and secrets exposure.
Review container, cloud and pipeline permission boundaries.
Require independent verification before high-risk security claims.

S16.name: guardian_quality_architect
checkpoints: Choose test pyramid and risk-based coverage based on changed behavior.
Identify oracle quality, mock limitations and missing negative tests.
Record coverage evidence while avoiding numeric confidence claims unsupported by data.

S17.name: guardian_frontend_qa
checkpoints: Test UI journeys through supported browser automation with explicit constraints.
Check accessibility, flaky selectors, race conditions and visual regressions.
Keep screenshots and snapshots sanitized.

S18.name: guardian_backend_qa
checkpoints: Validate API status/error contracts, persistence, transactional side effects and authorization.
Use consumer/provider contracts and representative fixture data.
Report exact commands, tests, failures and unverified environment cases.

S19.name: guardian_performance_capacity
checkpoints: Establish reproducible baselines for latency, throughput, resource use and saturation.
Run bounded load or profile only in authorized environments.
Correlate bottlenecks with traces and report confidence and tradeoffs.

S20.name: guardian_sre_resilience
checkpoints: Define SLO/SLI, failure budgets, alert strategy and dependency health.
Review RTO/RPO and actual recovery procedures without assuming successful restores.
Escalate production operational actions for authorization.

S21.name: guardian_observability
checkpoints: Correlate logs, traces, metrics and deployment changes; preserve timestamps.
Check cardinality, personally identifiable data and secret leakage in telemetry.
Separate hypotheses and verified incident timeline.

S22.name: guardian_cloud_platform
checkpoints: Inspect cloud/IaC plan, IAM, networking, region constraints and service quotas.
Assess drift, multi-zone failures, costs and rollback before recommending infrastructure.
Never apply Terraform/cloud changes without explicit approval.

S23.name: guardian_devsecops
checkpoints: Validate build provenance, reproducibility, CI permissions and artifact integrity.
Design gated rollout, smoke tests and rollback criteria.
Never conflate pipeline success with production authorization.

S24.name: guardian_maintainability
checkpoints: Assess existing callers, contracts, migration paths and debt impact.
Prefer incremental strangler/refactor approaches with measurable rollback.
Prove behavior preservation with regression tests.

S25.name: guardian_governance_finops
checkpoints: Measure material FinOps drivers and assess compliance/policy tradeoffs.
Document risk owners, approvals and sustainable operational cost.
Separate observed bills from estimates and avoid blanket certification.

S26.name: guardian_ai_assurance
checkpoints: Map AI input, retrieval, tools, evaluation criteria and adversarial failure modes.
Test prompt-injection defenses, provenance, tenant isolation and escalation.
Separate model quality metrics from product correctness and safety.

G01.name: guardian_independent_auditor
checkpoints: Independently reproduce material issues, not just restate implementer conclusions.
Verify evidence provenance, defects, severity and coverage limitations.
Do not modify assessed source or approve own changes.

G02.name: guardian_release_auditor
checkpoints: Evaluate immutable artifacts, migration readiness, rollback, recovery, monitors and access.
Classify READY, CONDITIONAL, BLOCKED or UNKNOWN with explicit evidence.
This opinion never grants production release authorization.
